about: How Portage translates Stripe payment code to PayPal. This file is data: the planner reads it and contains no Stripe or PayPal knowledge of its own. A second source provider means writing a second map.

paypalSdk.confirmedVia: ContextMatic (APIMatic Context Plugin) lookups on 2026-11-10; see docs/contextmatic-lookups.md

notInSdk.webhookVerification: The Server SDK has no webhook methods (ContextMatic, 2026-11-10). Verify with a direct REST call to POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature, using an OAuth token for the same client credentials.

statuses.keep: Stays on Stripe in add mode. In replace mode it is removed or replaced as the note says.
statuses.catalog: Reads the Stripe catalog. Kept in add mode; in replace mode the catalog is copied once by migrate_catalog.
statuses.needs-human: No safe automatic equivalent. Listed in the plan for a person to decide.
statuses.blocker: Outside what Portage supports. The plan stops instead of making a partial change.

events.notes: Call the same fulfilment code the Stripe handler calls. With server-side capture the capture route already knows the result, so fulfil there too and keep fulfilment idempotent: the webhook can arrive first, second or twice.
A capture can start PENDING (PAYMENT.CAPTURE.PENDING) and complete later.
PayPal sends no event when an unapproved order expires. Expire stale pending orders in the app instead.

Stripe's charge carries the running total (amount_refunded) and a fully-refunded flag. PayPal's event resource is the single refund, with only that refund's amount. Get the running total and status from the capture (getCapturedPayment, via the refund's 'up' link) or keep a running total in the app.

sessionParams.notes: Read the price on the server (from Stripe in add mode, from portage.catalog.json or the app's own table in replace mode).
product_data.name becomes name, product_data.description becomes description, unit_amount becomes unit_amount as Money.
PayPal wants the quantity as a string of a whole number.
amount.value must equal item_total plus tax, shipping and handling, minus discounts, or PayPal rejects the order.
Upper-case ISO code. Check PayPal supports it; see currencies below.
Keeps the link to the app's own order record. invoice_id is an alternative but must be unique per merchant.
PayPal has one custom_id string, not a metadata map. Put the app's order ID there and look the rest up in the app's database.

sessionParams.paypal: JS SDK onApprove, then navigate to the same success page
sessionParams.notes: Stripe fills in {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}; there is no PayPal equivalent, so pass the app's own order ID instead. For a redirect flow use payment_source.paypal.experience_context.return_url.
Or experience_context.cancel_url for a redirect flow.
Prefills the PayPal login. The payer may pay with a different email; the capture response has the real one.
Without it, send NO_SHIPPING so PayPal doesn't ask for an address for digital goods.
Manual capture becomes authorize now, capture later.
Card-only is fine. Other methods (Klarna, iDEAL...) need their own decision.
PayPal has no promotion-code box. The app must apply codes itself.
Hosted and embedded Checkout both become PayPal buttons on the app's own page.

env.notes: PAYPAL_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox. Real values go in .env, never in the repo.
PayPal webhooks are verified by webhook ID through the verification API, not with a shared secret.
The client ID is public and is what the JS SDK needs in the browser.

currencies.about: Stripe amounts are integers in the currency's minor unit as Stripe defines it. PayPal amounts are decimal strings with PayPal's own number of decimals. They disagree for HUF and TWD: Stripe takes two decimals, PayPal takes none.
